I'll help you add prod overlay changes to the knr-ops repository. Let me start by exploring the current structure.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">find . -type f -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | grep -E "(kustomization|overlay|base)" | head -20</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
<parameter name="arguments_alt">
<parameter name="command">pwd && ls -la</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">pwd && ls -la</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">find . -type d -name "overlays" -o -name "base" -o -name "clusters" -o -name "infra" 2>/dev/null</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me check the repository structure more directly.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">ls -la</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me check if we're in the right directory and see what files exist here.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">pwd && ls -R | head -50</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me check the git worktree status and explore the repository:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">git log --oneline -5 && echo "---" && ls -la</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

This appears to be a benchmark repository. Let me look for the knr-ops stack specifically:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">find . -type d -name "knr*" -o -type d -name "*overlay*" 2>/dev/null | head -20</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me list the top-level directories:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">ls -1</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me check if there's a specific location for stack implementations:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">find . -maxdepth 3 -type f -name "kustomization.yaml" 2>/dev/null</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

The repository structure isn't showing up. Let me look at the README or structure documents to understand the layout:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">find . -name "README*" -o -name "*.md" | grep -i "knr\|overlay" | head -10</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me take a different approach and check what's in the current directory structure without filtering:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">tree -L 3 -d 2>/dev/null || find . -maxdepth 3 -type d | sort</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

It seems the directory listing isn't returning output. Let me check the current working directory and file count:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">pwd && echo "Files:" && find . -type f | wc -l && echo "Directories:" && find . -type d | wc -l</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Let me try a simpler approach:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="tool_name">bash</parameter>
<parameter name="arguments">
<parameter name="command">ls .</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
</function_calls>

Can you clarify the location of the knr-ops repository? The current directory appears to be a git worktree of the iac-cd-bench benchmark repo. Is there a specific path within this repo where the knr-ops stack files are located, or should I create the structure to implement the task?
